articles.region: International Criminal Court, Burma, Illicit Drug Trafficking
articles.headline: OFAC Announces Settlement with Pegasus Worldwide Logistics, Designates International Criminal Court Entities, and Removes Burma-Related Designation
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has announced a settlement agreement with Pegasus Worldwide Logistics, a freight forwarding firm. Pegasus Worldwide Logistics has agreed to remit $175,015 to resolve its potential civil liability for four apparent violations of the Illicit Drug Trafficking Sanctions Regulations and six apparent violations of the Reporting, Procedures and Penalties Regulations.

The violations stemmed from Pegasus dealing in blocked property between September 2023 and February 2024 by facilitating the importation of a machine supplied by a designated company. Additionally, Pegasus failed to fully respond to an OFAC subpoena for six months. The settlement amount reflects OFAC's determination that the conduct was non-egregious and not voluntarily disclosed.

In separate actions, OFAC also issued several International Criminal Court-related General Licenses (GLs 13, 14, 15, and 16) authorizing various transactions, including those related to telecommunications, enterprise software, pension payments, and certain detainees. Concurrently, OFAC removed a Burma-related designation from its Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons (SDN) List.

articles.headline: OFAC Issues New General License Authorizing Russian Diesel Fuel Transactions
body: The Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has issued Russia-related General License (GL) 135, titled "Authorizing Transactions Related to the Sale, Delivery, Offloading, and Importation of Diesel Fuel of Russian Federation Origin." This new general license authorizes transactions otherwise prohibited by the Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations and the Ukraine-/Russia-Related Sanctions Regulations.

The authorization is valid through 12:01 a.m. eastern daylight time, April 7, 2027. This move comes as global diesel supplies remain tight, with U.S. distillate inventories significantly below the five-year seasonal range.

However, GL 135 explicitly states that it does not authorize any debit to an account on the books of a U.S. financial institution belonging to the Central Bank of the Russian Federation, the National Wealth Fund of the Russian Federation, or the Ministry of Finance.

articles.headline: OFAC Imposes New Iran-Related Designations, Issues General License, and Amends Russia-Related General License
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has announced new Iran-related designations as part of its ongoing efforts to counter the Iranian regime's shadow fleet network. Concurrently, OFAC issued Iran-related General License EE, which authorizes the wind down of transactions involving Samudra Marine Services Private Limited.

In addition to the Iran-related actions, OFAC also issued an amended Russia-related General License 13S. This amended license authorizes certain administrative transactions that were previously prohibited by Directive 4 under Executive Order 14024.

The new Iran-related designations include individuals such as Harishyam Hariharan Chundakattil and Ketan Manohar Kochikar, both from India, who are linked to Samudra Marine Services Private Limited under Executive Order 13846.

articles.headline: OFAC Announces Designations Removals and Updates, Publishes Iran-Related Alert and Amended FAQ
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has announced several designations removals and updates to its sanctions lists. These actions are part of OFAC's ongoing review and adjustment of its sanctions programs.
In conjunction with these updates, OFAC has also published an Iran-related OFAC Alert. This alert aims to provide guidance and highlight potential risks associated with transactions involving Iran.
Furthermore, an amended Iran-related Frequently Asked Question (FAQ) has been published, offering clarification on existing sanctions policies and their application.

articles.headline: OFAC Imposes New Counter Terrorism Designations
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has announced new designations under its Counter Terrorism authorities. These actions target individuals and entities involved in supporting terrorist activities.

The designations aim to disrupt financial networks and limit the ability of terrorist organizations to operate globally. OFAC continues to leverage its sanctions tools to combat the financing of terrorism.

Further details regarding the specific individuals and entities designated were not immediately available in the initial announcement but are expected to be reflected in updates to the Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) List.

articles.headline: OFAC Designates Iranian Entities and Transnational Criminal Organization, Issues Determination and Amended FAQ
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has announced new Iran-related designations and updates, alongside a designation targeting a transnational criminal organization. These actions are part of ongoing efforts to counter illicit financial activities and threats to U.S. national security.

Among the Iran-related designations are individuals such as Mehnoosh Poursaraf Hamedani and Ramin Keshvardoust, both linked to entities supporting the Iranian economy. Several entities, including Bonasol Group Co., Limited and Dominion Trading Group Limited, registered in Hong Kong, were also added to the SDN List under Iran-related authorities.

Additionally, OFAC designated the 'A7 Network' as a transnational criminal organization, operating across Russia, Kyrgyzstan, Nigeria, and Zimbabwe. OFAC also published a Determination Pursuant to Executive Order 13902, targeting the automotive and rail sectors of the Iranian economy, and an amended Iran-related Frequently Asked Question (FAQ 831).

articles.headline: OFAC Designates Counter Terrorism and Transnational Criminal Organizations, Removes Belarus, Counter Narcotics, and Libya Designations
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has announced new designations targeting individuals and entities involved in counter terrorism and transnational criminal organizations. These actions aim to disrupt illicit networks and safeguard the international financial system.

In a separate but related move, OFAC also announced the removal of several designations related to Belarus, counter narcotics, and Libya. These removals indicate a recalibration of sanctions policies in these areas.
The specific details of the new designations and removals are expected to be reflected in updates to OFAC's Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) List and other relevant sanctions lists.

articles.region: Counter Narcotics, Counter Terrorism, Iran, Non-Proliferation
articles.headline: OFAC Imposes Extensive Designations Across Counter Narcotics, Counter Terrorism, Iran, and Non-Proliferation Programs
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has announced a broad set of designations targeting individuals and entities under its Counter Narcotics, Counter Terrorism, Iran-related, and Non-Proliferation sanctions programs. This comprehensive action aims to disrupt various illicit activities and threats to U.S. national security.

Among the individuals added to the Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) List are Ali Fotowat Ahmady, an Iranian national with U.S. citizenship, designated under non-proliferation authorities and linked to Kavoshcom Asia R and D Group. Seyyed Asghar Alizadeh Tabatabai, an Iranian national in China, was also designated under non-proliferation and Iran-related financial sanctions.

The designations also include individuals associated with the Sinaloa Cartel, such as Ilia Elizabeth Felix Rivera and Hildegardo Gastelum Garcia, under counter narcotics and counter terrorism authorities. Waseem Pasha Tajammal from Pakistan was designated under non-proliferation and Iran-related financial sanctions, linked to the Ministry of Defense and Armed Forces Logistics.

articles.headline: OFAC Publishes Regulatory Amendments, New Cuba Sanctions Regulations, and Amended Cuba-Related FAQs
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has issued a rule to streamline its regulatory provisions, reorganizing multiple parts within the Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) and eliminating over 100 subparts. This initiative aims to make information on delegations of authority, recordkeeping, and reporting requirements more accessible.

Significantly, OFAC has published new Cuba Sanctions Regulations (CSR) at 31 C.F.R. Part 516, implementing Executive Order (E.O.) 14404 of May 1, 2026, which imposes sanctions on those responsible for repression in Cuba and threats to U.S. national security. These regulations prohibit indirect financial transactions with entities on the Cuba Restricted List, eliminate the "U-turn" general license, and restrict certain travel-related transactions.

Furthermore, OFAC has amended the Iranian Transactions and Sanctions Regulations to incorporate E.O. 13902, which imposes sanctions with respect to additional sectors of Iran. The agency also issued five new and 29 amended Cuba-related Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs 1271–1275) and an OFAC Alert titled "Expanded Sanctions Against Cuba," highlighting increased sanctions risks.

articles.headline: OFAC Issues Amended Venezuela General Licenses
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has issued amended Venezuela-related General Licenses (GLs). These amendments include GL 46E, "Authorizing Certain Activities Involving Venezuelan-Origin Oil or Petrochemical Products," and GL 48D, "Authorizing the Supply of Certain Items and Services to Venezuela."

Additionally, OFAC issued Venezuela-related General License 49B, which authorizes negotiations of and entry into contingent contracts for certain investment in Venezuela. These actions reflect ongoing adjustments to U.S. policy regarding Venezuela.

These amended general licenses continue to support efforts by U.S. businesses to reinvest in Venezuela, aiming to strengthen U.S. national security in the Western Hemisphere and help restore Venezuela as a responsible and prosperous ally. The GLs still require dispute resolution proceedings to occur in the United States, United Kingdom, France, or Singapore.

articles.headline: Pegasus Worldwide Logistics Settles with OFAC for $175,015 in Sanctions Violations
body: Pegasus Worldwide Logistics has agreed to pay $175,015 to the U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) to settle its potential civil liability for apparent violations of sanctions regulations. The settlement addresses four apparent violations of the Illicit Drug Trafficking Sanctions Regulations and six apparent violations of the Reporting, Procedures and Penalties Regulations.

The violations involved Pegasus dealing in blocked property by facilitating the importation of a machine supplied by a designated company between September 2023 and February 2024. Additionally, Pegasus failed to fully respond to an OFAC subpoena for six months.
OFAC determined that Pegasus's conduct was non-egregious and not voluntarily disclosed, leading to the agreed-upon settlement amount.

articles.headline: Individual Fined $1.4 Million by OFAC for Providing Services to Iranian Software Company
body: An individual has agreed to pay $1,427,230 to the U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) to settle potential civil liability for providing management consulting and advisory services to a leading Iranian software company. The individual also received Iranian-origin dividends into U.S. bank accounts.
This enforcement action highlights OFAC's continued focus on individuals and entities that facilitate transactions or provide services to sanctioned Iranian entities, even indirectly.

The settlement underscores the importance of due diligence and adherence to U.S. sanctions regulations, particularly when engaging in international business or financial activities that may involve sanctioned jurisdictions.

articles.headline: Global Trade Reaches Record $35 Trillion in 2025, Driven by AI Investment and Supply Chain Adaptations
body: Global trade reached a record $35 trillion in 2025, with higher trade values in 2026 being driven by price increases amid an ongoing energy shock. The UN trade and development agency, UNCTAD, reported that developing countries face new technological and policy barriers that hinder their greater participation in the global economy.

The World Trade Organization (WTO) sharply raised its 2026 global merchandise trade volume growth forecast from 1.9% to 3.9%, projecting 4.1% growth in 2027. This upgrade is largely attributed to supply chain adaptations in response to the Middle East conflict and a significant boost from AI-related investment.

Semiconductors, servers, and other AI-enabled products contributed 47% of goods trade growth in the first half of 2026, with their trade value surging 67% year-on-year. While AI-enabled products account for less than 15% of global trade, they contributed nearly half of the incremental growth.

articles.headline: Middle East Conflicts Intensify: Strait of Hormuz Remains Closed, Yemen War Reignites
body: Multiple conflicts are simultaneously escalating across the Middle East, with significant global implications for oil prices, shipping, and travel. More than seven months after U.S.-Israeli strikes began on February 28, 2026, the Strait of Hormuz remains largely closed, with traffic down by approximately 95%.

The war in Yemen has reignited following the collapse of a truce in July 2026. Houthi forces have advanced in Taiz Governorate and claimed missile and drone strikes on a Saudi Aramco facility in Riyadh on October 3. In response, Yemen's Saudi-backed government launched a major offensive on October 4.

In the Israeli-Palestinian conflict, the Security Council is holding its quarterly open debate on "The situation in the Middle East, including the Palestinian question." This comes one year after Israel and Hamas agreed to a U.S.-brokered "Comprehensive Plan to End the Gaza Conflict," though the second and third phases of the plan, including Hamas' disarmament and IDF withdrawal, have not yet been implemented.
articles.source: Al Jazeera / The Jerusalem Post / ISW

articles.headline: Russia-Ukraine War Enters Fifth Year, NATO Reports Russian Submarine Activity Near Arctic Cables
body: The conflict between Russia and Ukraine has entered its fifth year, with Russia continuing to target bridges and cities across Ukraine. The United States has proposed new three-way talks in the UAE to address the ongoing hostilities.

In a separate but related development, NATO has reported tracking and driving off Russian submarines that were reportedly practicing attacks on undersea cables near Norway's Svalbard islands. This activity highlights a "hidden front" in Europe, raising concerns about potential hybrid attacks on critical infrastructure.

These geopolitical tensions in Europe are contributing to a complex global landscape, impacting energy markets and international relations. The ongoing conflicts are feeding into each other, creating a challenging environment for stability and security.

articles.headline: Revisions to the Entity List
body: In this rule, the Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) revises the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) by removing two addresses associated with Arrow Electronics (Hong Kong) Co., Ltd. from the Entity List under the destination of China, People's Republic of (China). This determination follows the removal from the Entity List of Arrow China Electronics Trading Co., Ltd., and the removal of six aliases for Arrow Electronics (Hong Kong) Co., Ltd. in November 2025.

articles.headline: Removal From the Entity List
body: In this rule, the Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) amends the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) by removing one entity from the Entity List under the destination of Turkey.

articles.headline: Streamlining Export Controls for Drone Exports
body: The Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is easing export controls on certain Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs or drones) and related parts, components, accessories, attachments, technology, and software under the Export Administration Regulations (EAR). Specifically, this rule: eliminates wind gust tolerance as a parameter for determining UAV controls under the EAR; increases the threshold for national security controls on certain UAVs from an endurance of 30 minutes to an endurance of 3 hours; makes conforming changes to remove national security controls on software and technology associated with UAVs with an endurance less than 3 hours; maintains military end-use and end-user controls on those lower endurance drones and associated software and technology; clarifies Commerce Control List (CCL) controls for certain UAVs specially designed for military use; and removes national security controls on certain specially designed parts, components, accessories, and attachments for such UAVs as they do not provide any significant military or intelligence capabilities.

articles.headline: Implementation of EAR Export Controls on Silencers, Mufflers, and Sound Suppressors; and Other Firearms Related Changes
body: The Department of Commerce (Commerce), Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is revising the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) and the Commerce Control List (CCL) to appropriately control certain silencers, mufflers, and sound suppressors (sound suppressors) that will no longer be described on the International Traffic in Arms Regulations U.S. Munitions List (USML). This interim final rule (IFR) complements a Department of State interim final rule published elsewhere in this issue of the Federal Register (International Traffic in Arms Regulations: USML Category I Firearm Suppressors (1400-AG11) (State IFR)). This transfer of jurisdiction will reduce the regulatory burden on exports of sound suppressors. This IFR also revises the EAR to allow firearms and related items to be temporarily exported and reexported under a license exception as tools of trade, thereby relieving exporters of the regulatory burden of applying for authorization. Finally, this IFR clarifies which items fall within the scope of the EAR's entry clearance requirements for a temporary import.

articles.headline: Enhanced Favorable Treatment for the United Arab Emirates Under the Export Administration Regulations
body: In this final rule, the Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) amends the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) to provide enhanced favorable treatment for the United Arab Emirates (UAE). Specifically, BIS is removing the UAE from Country Groups D:3 and D:4 and adding the UAE to Country Group A:5. More license exceptions will now be available, including Strategic Trade Authorization (STA) for the UAE Government and approved commercial entities in the UAE. STA will authorize the export, reexport, or transfer (in-country) of military items; certain commercial satellites and spacecraft; and dual-use items useful in, inter alia, oil and gas production, desalination, and civil nuclear power generation. The UAE Government and approved commercial entities will also have license-free access to advanced computing items, consistent with the May 2025 U.S.-UAE Artificial Intelligence Cooperation framework, without compromising U.S. digital infrastructure buildout.
